text:
For pure budgeting features and granular saving pots, Monzo is the top overall choice in the UK, followed closely by Starling Bank for everyday simplicity and Chase UK if you want higher interest rates and cashback alongside your pots.   
era.app

Bank	Pot Name	Key Budgeting & Pot Features	Interest & Perks	Best For
Monzo	Pots	

• Pay direct debits & standing orders directly from a dedicated Bills Pot.




• Salary Sorter automatically splits payday funds into pots.




• Virtual cards linked to specific pots (on paid plans from £3/mo).

	

• Up to 3.45%–3.65% AER on instant/limited-access pots (varies by tier).




• Round-ups with optional 2x/5x/10x multipliers (paid plans).

	Granular automation and ring-fencing bills so you never accidentally spend rent money.
Starling Bank	Spaces	

• Pay bills directly from a Space using a dedicated virtual card (free).




• Round-ups into a chosen Space.




• Clean spending categorization without upsells.

	

• No paid tiers—all budgeting and virtual card features are free.




• Fee-free spending abroad.

	Zero-fee simplicity and free virtual cards tied to specific budgets (e.g., groceries or travel).
Chase UK	Saver & Spending Accounts	

• Open multiple separate current accounts (up to 20) with their own account numbers and toggle your debit card between them.




• Round-ups go into a dedicated 5% AER account.

	

• 4.75% AER boosted saver rate.




• 1%–2% cashback on everyday debit card spending.

	Maximising returns—earning high interest and cashback while keeping spending separated.
Revolut	Pockets	

• Auto-sort salary into Pockets.




• Link external UK bank accounts to view all spending in one place (free).

	

• ~3.15% AER on standard savings.




• Strong multi-currency tools and bill splitting.

	Multi-bank tracking and frequent travellers.
Which one should you pick?

Choose Monzo if you want the most comprehensive budgeting ecosystem. Its Salary Sorter and Bills Pots make zero-based budgeting effortless, though features like custom categories, external bank syncing, and virtual cards require Monzo Extra (£3/month).   
Money To The Masses

Choose Starling if you refuse to pay a monthly fee. You get free virtual cards linked to specific Spaces (great for capping takeaway or shopping budgets) and full FSCS protection without constant prompts to upgrade.

Choose Chase if you care more about interest and cashback than deep spending analytics. Because each pot is technically its own current account with a sort code and account number, you can set up direct debits from individual pots while earning higher interest on your savings.

(Note: Monzo, Starling, and Chase are all fully licensed UK banks with £85,000 FSCS deposit protection; Revolut operates under specific UK banking/e-money transitional rules depending on account migration.)
